subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native batch file/search tool inputs, AI-callable context block load/unload tools, and strict submitted-plan enforcement as core runtime surfaces, and if so which track should be designed first?
rationale: These changes add new core tool schemas, persisted context/session semantics, and runner policy/config behavior; automation should not choose those product and compatibility contracts.

options.title: Split Into Three Design Tracks
options.body: Keep the umbrella open but require separate maintainer-approved designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Implement One Narrow Track First
options.body: Choose one subproblem, such as recoverable context clearing, and defer the other two until product direction is clearer.

options.title: Decline Core Runtime Changes
options.body: Keep current parallel tool calls, context engine, compaction, and update_plan behavior and route extra orchestration to plugins or skills.

recommendation.title: Split Into Three Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open but require separate maintainer-approved designs for batching, context lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the prior keep-open product review and has the strongest adjacent planning/runtime-tool history among the traced owners.
